Welcome to Brent Knoll School
Brent Knoll School is a Co-operative Trust special school for children aged 4–17 with complex social, communication and interaction difficulties, including autism. Located in the London Borough of Lewisham, we recognise the importance of meeting the needs of SEND pupils (special educational needs and disability) in this context while celebrating its diversity and our young people’s place within it.
The school seeks to creatively deliver curriculum solutions that ensure the pathways for learners are well-defined and tailored to their individual needs. The implementation of the curriculum provides them with the necessary skills to move on and take their places at appropriate destinations after Brent Knoll. By developing their independence and allowing them to become engaged and active citizens in a rapidly changing world, we can positively impact their life chances.

Headteacher’s Welcome
I am extremely proud and privileged to welcome you as Headteacher of Brent Knoll School.
I lead a highly committed, talented, and dedicated staff team who provide the very best education for our young people.
We are a Co-operative Trust special school for children aged 4–17 with complex social, communication and interaction difficulties, including autism.
Situated in the London Borough of Lewisham, we are a diverse community and welcome students from many different backgrounds. We celebrate our diversity and learn from each other, valuing each student as unique and special.
Our holistic, pupil-centred approach to educating our young people, ensures that enrichment, therapeutic interventions and a bespoke, personalised curriculum develops their independence, provides them with the necessary skills and allows them to become engaged and active citizens in a rapidly changing world which positively impacts their life chances.
We are outward facing and value the collaborative partnerships we have with families and the wider community, as these are key to supporting our young people:
‘Be the best that we can be’
As a school community we are committed to our school’s core values and our pupils and staff are encouraged to live these values in all aspects of school life:
Fairness • Honesty • Kindness • Respect • Responsibility
I look forward to meeting you when you visit the school and wish your child every success and happiness in their time with us.

Aims Ethos And Equality
Brent Knoll School – our vision statement
The Brent Knoll community will:
‘Be the best that we can be.’
The government emphasises that schools are required to ensure that key ‘British Values’ are taught in all UK schools. The government set out its definition of British values in the ‘Prevent Strategy’. These values include:
Brent Knoll School, along with all primary and secondary schools in Lewisham, have signed Lewisham’s pledge to tackle race inequalities in education.
We will work to address the inequalities that result from historic, systemic racist policies and practices.
We pledge to take actions that will address access and opportunity for all pupils, by highlighting inequalities and increasing awareness.
Why is this work needed?
Evidence shows us there are historic, systemic inequalities in the education system – not just in Lewisham, but in London and across the UK.
Statistics show us that certain demographic groups have lower educational attainment and a higher exclusion rate than others.
This has an impact in the future – in particular, young men of Black Caribbean and dual heritage (Black Caribbean/White) often experience poorer educational outcomes.
This shows us that historically, we have been failing certain groups of young people. This is something we cannot ignore, because we want all of our young people to achieve their potential.
We know there are many factors that lead to these outcomes. Education and the wider support that a school community can provide is one of these factors. This is something we can work to improve.
How does this affect my child?
We know that no single initiative will bring about change, but the changes we introduce will create lasting transformation in the lives of our young people. We know that these improvements to our education system will be beneficial to all Lewisham children, irrespective of their background.
It is likely that a lot of this work will go unnoticed by your child, as it will be ‘behind the scenes’ in terms of teacher training and policy work.
But in time, this will filter down into the language used, subjects studied, books that are brought home, conversations that you are having with your child about their school day. It will ultimately result in a more representative curriculum in Lewisham schools which reflects the diverse community we are proud to be part of.

Brent Knoll and Watergate Co-operative Trust
Brent Knoll and Watergate Co-Operative Trust is a grassroots, parent-led exempt charity in the borough of Lewisham. The Trust supports children and young people with SEND and profound and complex learning and physical disabilities as well as their families and carers.
The Trust was formed in 2012 with the intention of providing support to parents and carers of the two schools along with developing the provision for SEND in the wider community. A visioning exercise identified short term aims of developing holiday provision, providing support and information for parents and carers relating to SEND and providing opportunities for collaboration between the two schools.
We are currently working with a fundraiser who has been successful in securing funds to support Easter, summer and half term break holiday schemes which run at the two schools.
For more information about the Brent Knoll and Watergate Co-operative Trust please email:
info@bkwgtrust.org.uk or visit the website bkwgtrust.org.uk
Call Us Today

Careers & Guidance
At Brent Knoll School, we are committed to ensuring that all students are fully supported and guided through the process of planning their futures. By providing high quality and impartial education programmes, information, advice and guidance for all students from Years 7 -11, we believe our students are well prepared for the future and are ready to progress on to appropriate courses or employment after leaving the school.
All staff at Brent Knoll play an active role in preparing our students for the future. We have a full career education programme that is delivered through PHSE, special events, enrichment programmes, visits, trips and assemblies, as well as our own enterprise project.
We are very proud of our extensive and strong links with employers. These employers work closely with our students through work placements, visits, talks, interview preparation, careers fairs and work-related learning events.

Out Of School Hours Learning
At Brent Knoll School, we are committed to offering a wide range of non-statutory, out-of-hours learning opportunities to all of our pupils who wish to access them. The activities and groups are carefully considered and planned to ensure suitability for all individuals and meet the diverse needs of our pupils.
Club groups are rotated and reviewed each half term so that as many pupils as possible get the chance to take part.

Breakfast Club
Pupils are provided with a healthy breakfast and supported to develop the skills necessary to prepare this independently.
Duke of Edinburgh Award
Brent Knoll offers many of our Key Stage 4 pupils the opportunity to work towards both the Bronze and Silver Duke of Edinburgh awards. Pupils are required to take part in voluntary work, sporting activity and expeditions. This highly regarded accredited course encourages independence, confidence and high aspirations.
Football Club
Delivered by a qualified Football Association coach, pupils learn and practise new skills as well as engaging in good natured competitive competition.
Travel Training
Brent Knoll is an accredited centre for training young people in safe travel. Pupils learn about using public transport safely and work towards being able to travel independently.

Safeguarding
Safeguarding at Brent Knoll
At Brent Knoll School we have a primary responsibility for the care, welfare and safety of all pupils in our charge. We are committed to providing help and support to meet the needs of children as soon as problems emerge, protecting children from maltreatment, whether that is within or outside the home, including online, preventing impairment of children’s mental and physical health or development and ensuring that children grow up in circumstances consistent with the provision of safe and effective care.
We encourage a culture in which all staff believe safeguarding to be of the highest importance and understand that their vigilance is critical. We want all staff to feel confident to discuss their concerns with designated staff/Governors and have clear lines of protocol in place for how to do this.
At Brent Knoll School we explicitly teach pupils about safeguarding themselves in and outside of school, including online, through a broad and balanced curriculum. We establish and maintain a culture in which children feel secure, are encouraged to talk and are listened to.
If you are a new visitor to the school, please ensure that you bring a valid form of identification e.g. driving licence.

Additional Support
In order to meet the needs of our pupils, Brent Knoll School offers a variety of school-based therapies and additional support while working closely with a number of outside agencies. School-based therapies provide children and young people with SEND improved access to education by supporting:
The wide range of needs of children and young people at Brent Knoll requires different levels and types of provision. This means that support might be best provided for entire groups or classes, such as whole school training or class intervention approaches, working in collaboration with school staff. On the other hand, more specific support may be required and is delivered through individual or small group targeted intervention approaches also in collaboration with school staff. In addition, specialist interventions may be necessary for those who require a highly individualised and personalised programme of work.

Admissions
Admissions to Brent Knoll School are governed by the Special Educational Needs Code of Practice. Pupils are admitted to Brent Knoll following an assessment of their special educational needs. If the assessment results in a Statement of Special Educational Needs or an Education, Health and Care Plan that indicates a placement at Brent Knoll might be appropriate, Lewisham Education Authority asks us to consider whether or not we feel we can meet a child’s needs. All referrals are considered by senior staff and the pupil is visited at their current setting if necessary. Following careful consideration of all the evidence, a decision will be made as to whether or not we feel Brent Knoll can meet their special educational needs.
The decision to place a child at Brent Knoll is made by the Lewisham SEN placement panel. While we attempt to maintain optimal numbers in each year group, we can be directed to admit pupils over this number by the local authority or a SEND tribunal. We encourage all prospective parents to visit the school at one of our regular Open Mornings. Attendance is by appointment only, and parents should contact the school office for dates and times. The final decision on placement at Brent Knoll rests with the SEN placement panel. Prior to admission, the school will arrange a series of visits or events to prepare the young person for the transition to Brent Knoll. During this time, parents will be invited into school to complete the admissions form, consent forms and the home-school agreement.

Governors have an executive role in policy development, the appointment of the headteacher and the hearing of appeals from both staff and parents. Chair of Governors, Parent Governor
Laura Deitz
It is a privilege to serve as Chair of Governors at Brent Knoll School. My eldest daughter has been part of Brent Knoll since Reception and is now in Year 8, and through her journey I have seen first-hand the transformative impact of this community.
When she was diagnosed with autism at the age of two, I quickly became involved in volunteering with charities and community organisations supporting children with additional needs, along with their families and carers. That work, alongside my professional background in finance, has shaped my commitment to ensuring that every child is given the opportunity to thrive, regardless of the challenges they face.
As a parent of three other young daughters, I am deeply grateful that Lily is growing up in a school where she is understood, encouraged, and celebrated. Brent Knoll is a uniquely nurturing community—one where children flourish, parents are supported, and staff are deeply dedicated. As Chair, my focus is to uphold that spirit: to listen, to strengthen the partnership between school and families, and to help ensure every pupil can reach their full potential. It is a joy to spend time in the school, to see the progress of our students, and to be part of such a special community.

I joined Brent Knoll’s Governing Body as I wanted to put my knowledge and skills of working in the health and social care sector to good use, particularly my expertise in reviewing and commissioning children and young people’s services and addressing inequalities.
I work in south-east London as a children’s services senior manager jointly for a local authority and the NHS. I use my knowledge of public sector procurement and education commissioning to support the school run efficiently and achieve value for money, making sure that every penny is maximised and benefits our learners.
I really enjoy being a member of the Governing Body for Brent Knoll, and I am committed to supporting our learners having access to the right support at the right time. I am also a firm believer that all decisions made at a Governing Body level should be in the best interest and wellbeing of pupils, putting them firmly at the centre of the decision-making process.
Staff Governor and Music Co-Ordinator
Gina Evans
Staff Governor since March 2024
I am proud to serve as the staff representative on the Governing Body at Brent Knoll School, where I have the privilege of working alongside a dedicated team committed to ensuring our pupils receive the very best education, experiences, and memories during their school years.
Since joining Brent Knoll in 2015 as the school’s Music Teacher, I have expanded my role to become Music Co-ordinator, the school’s Makaton Tutor, and a Middle Leader. One of my proudest achievements has been developing the Makaton Choir and Mini Makaton Singers, creating countless opportunities for our pupils to perform both within the school and in the wider community. These experiences have not only enriched our students’ lives but also created lasting memories for staff and families alike.
As a Makaton Tutor, I have also introduced a variety of initiatives for Brent Knoll families, education staff, and the wider Lewisham community. These events have been highly successful, both in sharing specialist knowledge to support those living and working with people with special educational needs, and in building meaningful connections through shared experiences. In my role as Staff Governor, I continue to develop my understanding of school governance and leadership. I particularly enjoy exploring ways to strengthen partnerships that further enrich the lives of our pupils, their families, our staff, and the local community.

My previous role at the Department for Education involved close collaboration with schools and Trusts across London and the Southeast, particularly through work in Education Estates.
As a resident of SE London, I’m committed to supporting inclusive, high-quality education in my community. I bring a broad understanding of school systems and policy to my role at Brent Knoll, and I’m dedicated to helping the Governing Body make effective, evidence-based decisions.
I passionately believe every child deserves the best possible start in life and every opportunity possible. I’m proud to support Brent Knoll’s mission to help every pupil thrive and reach their full potential.

I’m honoured to be a School Governor at Brent Knoll School, where I have served as a co-opted governor since 2024. I am a Digital Marketing Manager with experience across a wide range of industries, from education to life sciences, with a particular specialism in biotechnology.
As a mother of two young children under the age of five, I bring a strong parent perspective to my role and a deep appreciation of the importance of early support, inclusion, and advocacy for children with additional needs. I’m passionate about combining my educational background, professional expertise, and lived experience to support the work of the school.
Living within the borough has strengthened my commitment to the local community and to equality, diversity, and inclusion. Growing up, I was unaware that governance roles like this existed, and I recognise that many families from similar backgrounds may not see themselves represented in these spaces. I’m proud to contribute as part of a collaborative governing team, working in the best interests of pupils and their families.

I was delighted to become a Brent Knoll governor in summer 2025. I am the link governor for careers and personal development.
I wanted to contribute to the Brent Knoll and Lewisham community in this role as I care very much about the quality of education and opportunities for all children and young people in our society. At work, I monitor delivery of policies at the Department for Education. I use performance data and methods such as surveys and focus groups to understand delivery at a national level. My prior experience working on special educational needs and disabilities transformation programmes in local authorities, as well as working directly with local authority social care teams, gives me a broader understanding of Brent Knoll’s context. In these earlier roles I built project management and community engagement skills.
I hope to put all of my experience to use at Brent Knoll, and I know that I will learn a lot from students and staff while I serve as a governor.
Foundation Governor & Safeguarding Link Governor
Salma N. Moolji
I am honoured to join Brent Knoll as a school governor. As a parent of young children, I value a school setting that promotes equitable and safe education for all. I believe that children should have quality care and education that is sensitive to their needs, and that schools like Brent Knoll are important for accessing independence alongside learning. I also live in SE London and wish to participate in the community and institutions around me.
In my current role, I lead a strategic sustainability function in a finance company. Previously, I worked in impact investing including into educational settings in emerging markets like Sierra Leone and Afghanistan, giving me valuable insight into the importance of strong governance and collaboration. I believe my management and functional leadership skills, as well as technical knowledge on environmental and social sustainability can contribute to a well-rounded view that is aligned with Brent Knoll’s ethos and holistic approach to learning.

I am a local resident and public sector consultant bringing governance experience from policy roles across various Whitehall departments, along with knowledge of local government & communications from time spent working for a South London MP.
I feel privileged to have been nominated to the role of governor at Brent Knoll and look forward to adopting the shared role of Link Governor for Safeguarding later in the year, as well as working closely with staff, families and my fellow governors to ensure Brent Knoll continues to be the safe, excellent and inspiring place that it is.

School Facilities
Our new school building opened in September 2015. We were privileged to be given the opportunity to design a bespoke learning environment for all our children and young people. We took an uncompromising approach to create a calm, nurturing and safe space where all learners can achieve their potential.
Plans were painstakingly designed, adjusted and adapted to create the highest quality built environment, which our pupils deserve. Based both on current research into the impact of the built environment on the wellbeing of children and young people with communication and interaction difficulties and our own experience of maximising the use of available space, we created a building that has become internationally renowned.
In 2017, our school building was shortlisted for the prestigious Architects’ Journal School Building of the Year Award. We were the only specialist setting and the only state-funded school to be shortlisted.
The National Autistic Society highlighted our building as having been “designed with great sensitivity to the needs of people with autism.”
We continually strive to improve our built environment and are constantly looking for ways to enhance and maximise the spaces, both internal and external, including the pursuit of sustainability.

Eyfs Curriculum
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
At Brent Knoll School we believe that the Early Years and Foundation Stage (EYFS) is integral to providing the building blocks for children’s life-long learning and development. Through purposeful and meaningful play alongside real-life experiences, children consolidate and contextualise their learning. Children are encouraged to ‘have a go’ at new things and take risks while we nurture their self-confidence, allowing them to become the best that they can be.
The EYFS Curriculum
The EYFS curriculum is carefully planned with an emphasis on purposeful play and real-life experiences through a balance of adult-led and child-initiated activities that reflect the special educational needs of our pupils. The EYFS curriculum details the topics that are taught through a cross-curricular approach.
EYFS Policy
The EYFS policy details the expectations within the EYFS along with the relevant legislation and acts as a guide to ensure the EYFS curriculum continues to provide outstanding learning and development.

Brent Knoll Sixth form
What is our sixth form?
A one-year transition course for students who would benefit from additional time within a nurturing environment. We develop student’s confidence and independence with a view to them transitioning to a local Further Education College enabling them to become active citizens, able to participate and make a positive contribution within their own communities.
What is our curriculum?
The curriculum provides a breadth of experiences and enables personalised learning to ensure that each learner can progress and develop at their own pace. As well as opportunities to experience new learning opportunities there is a desire to allow consolidation and broadening of previous knowledge and experience to help develop their life skills, encourage independence and get a taste of the world of employment developing their social, communication and interaction skills.
